Agent Name: Planner
, Step Number: 1
, Reason for Mistake: The Planner incorrectly identified option B ("a bulldozer pushing soil") as the best example of physical weathering. Physical weathering (mechanical weathering) is defined as the physical breakdown of rocks and minerals into smaller pieces by natural forces (like temperature changes, frost wedging, or abrasion by wind/water) without changing their chemical composition. While a bulldozer does mechanically break soil/rock, it is an anthropogenic (human-made) activity, not a natural geological process. In the context of standard earth science education questions, "physical weathering" refers to natural phenomena. Option C ("ice fracturing a stone," referring to frost wedging) is the classic, correct example of natural physical weathering. Option A is biological weathering (decay), and Option D is chemical weathering. The Planner failed to distinguish between human mechanical action and natural geological weathering processes.
